scope: Candidate rules for resolving recurring disagreements between two independent ranked Luna topic-classification passes.
global_constraints: Apply ontology definition, include_when, exclude_when and prompt_logic_note before any rule.
Rules may resolve only the disputed pathway or role unless a shared assignment contains a substantial ontology error.
Do not infer substantive topics from title alone.
Never resolve by blind union, blind intersection, or systematic preference for Pass A or Pass B.
Preserve raw Pass A, raw Pass B, rule applied, final decision, rationale and evidence status.

rules.trigger: Abstract/full text evidence is unavailable or insufficient to apply ontology criteria.
rules.action: Do not adjudicate topic pathways from title alone.

rules.trigger: A disputed Methods pathway is proposed because the study uses a laboratory, diagnostic, statistical or modelling method.
rules.action: Retain a Methods pathway only when development, validation, comparison or review of the method is itself a principal contribution. Otherwise retain the substantive-domain pathway(s) supported by the ontology.

rules.trigger: V3_001 is disputed and one or more specific environmental pathways are clearly substantive.
rules.action: Exclude V3_001 when the specific environmental issue(s) can be coded directly and no broad multi-issue framework is independently substantive. Retain V3_001 only when several environmental issues are treated collectively and no specific issue dominates, as required by the ontology.

rules.trigger: A pathway is disputed because one pass treats an outcome/response as independently substantive and the other treats it as incidental.
rules.action: Retain as SECONDARY when the concept is an explicit objective, intervention, exposure, outcome or conclusion and independently satisfies the ontology. Exclude when it is only a routine measurement, covariate, validation target or background/context.

rules.trigger: Both passes assign the same pathway but disagree on PRIMARY versus SECONDARY.
rules.action: Assign PRIMARY only if the pathway is central to the paper's main research question, intervention, exposure, outcome or conclusion; assign SECONDARY if independently substantive but not central. Multiple PRIMARY assignments are allowed only when genuinely co-primary.

rules.trigger: A disputed pathway appears only in motivation, background, market/context description, policy aspiration or discussion rather than as an analysed question/outcome.
rules.action: Exclude the contextual pathway unless it independently satisfies the ontology inclusion criteria.

rules.trigger: V3_023 is disputed and companies themselves are substantive units of analysis.
rules.action: Retain V3_023 when companies or industry structure are substantive units of analysis, even if ownership/concentration is not the narrow subject; exclude when firms are merely mentioned as suppliers, funders or contextual actors.

rules.trigger: A record substantively analyses both an escape event/cause and what happens after escape.
rules.action: Retain V3_011 for quantified/explained escape occurrence/causes and V3_013 for substantive post-escape survival, dispersal, establishment or impacts. Allow both PRIMARY when both are central.

rules.trigger: Both passes agree on a pathway and role.
rules.action: Preserve the shared assignment unless it clearly violates an ontology exclusion rule, clearly fails the ontology inclusion/definition criteria, or is materially misclassified. Any override must be explicitly documented.

validation_gate.sample_source: Fresh A/B disagreement records not used to derive these rules.
validation_gate.blinded_manual_reference: Manual ontology-first adjudication completed without seeing candidate rule output where practicable.
required_metrics: exact pathway-set agreement with manual adjudication
validation_gate.acceptance_principle: Do not promote candidate rules to production unless validation shows they materially reduce manual review without introducing systematic ontology errors. Thresholds must be agreed before evaluating the independent sample.
